subtype: Approach: balancing career with family and health values [Thinking]
passage: I'm Tanuja, twenty-five, and last month I finally wrote down what the next five years must hold besides work. My parents in Nashik are getting older, and I want to be within a few hours of them. Marriage is something my family raises and I might want in three or four years, so I shouldn't plan as if I'll never have time for it. And I keep skipping my morning walk when deadlines pile up. I said all this to Preeti over lunch, and saying it made it clearer. So the plan gets its limits first: weekends mostly free, one trip home a month, a walk I protect. Then I ask which jobs fit inside those limits. If a role can't, it isn't on the list.

qa.q: What is Tanuja worried about when deadlines pile up?
qa.a: Tanuja worries about health slipping, shown by skipping the morning walk again and again when work gets heavy.

qa.q: What could Tanuja try if a good job does not fit the limits?
qa.a: Tanuja could ask someone in that job how they manage their time, or test the role with a short trial, since that shows whether it can bend without eating into family and health.

qa.q: How might Tanuja's parents see the limit of one trip home a month?
qa.a: They would probably feel valued and less worried, because the plan puts staying close to them ahead of the fastest promotion.

grounding: Shows a person weighing marriage, ageing parents and health, and setting work limits so the career plan fits around life.

subtype: Approach: balancing career with family and health values [Thinking]
passage:
Coaching note, session 3.
Disha arrived with her five-year plan, which last month had been only job titles. Today it had a second column she called 'Life'. In it: marriage, probably in two years; her parents in Indore, her father's knees getting worse; and her own back pain from long sitting, which her doctor had asked her to take seriously.
She had then set limits beside each career goal. The promotion to team lead stays, but not through constant weekend work: one weekend a month at most. A trip to Indore every quarter goes into the calendar before project deadlines do. A walk every lunch break.
She said, 'Last year my career plan ate everything else.' I've asked her to try the limits for three months and bring back what held and what broke.
Suraj

qa.q: What did Disha call the second column?
What does Disha's line 'my career plan ate everything else' suggest she felt last year?
qa.a: It suggests she felt drained and regretful, as if work had crowded out her family and health.

qa.q: What else could Disha do if a deadline clashes with an Indore trip?
qa.a: She could decide in advance which one wins and tell her manager early, so the limit isn't broken in the moment.

qa.q: How might Disha's parents be affected by the quarterly trips?
qa.a: They get regular visits they can count on, which matters more as her father's knees worsen.

grounding: It shows a coach's note on someone who adds marriage, ageing parents and health to a career plan and sets limits like no constant weekend work.

subtype: Approach: balancing career with family and health values [Thinking]
passage:
Tuesday, 11 p.m.
Missed Nandini's cousin's engagement on Sunday for a release. Third family event this year. Amma called tonight and didn't complain, which was worse.
So I sat down with my career plan and did what I should have done in January: wrote down what else matters. Nandini and I want to marry next winter. Amma and Appa are both over sixty-five. My sleep is a mess, and I haven't played badminton in eight months.
New rules, next to the career goals: no work on Sundays except real incidents. Leave on time on Wednesdays for badminton. Two trips home a year, booked in January like any deadline.
The promotion can take a year longer. I'd rather get there with people still around me.
Suraj

qa.q: Which evening does Suraj plan to leave on time for badminton?
Why did Amma not complaining feel worse to Suraj?
qa.a: Suraj felt guilty and sad, sensing that Amma had stopped expecting Suraj to show up.

qa.q: What else could help Suraj keep the Sunday rule?
qa.a: Suraj could tell the team lead about it and agree what counts as a real incident, so the rule is respected.

qa.q: How might Nandini see these new rules?
qa.a: Nandini may feel relieved and valued, seeing their wedding and family placed alongside the promotion.

grounding: It shows someone weighing marriage plans, ageing parents and health, and setting limits like no Sunday work so the career plan supports life.
